reflect_args: ^^nb::instantiate_<^^absl::InlinedVector, with_<^^int, val_<size_t(4)>>, with_<^^double, val_<size_t(2)>>, with_<^^std::string, val_<size_t(4)>>>
subset.rationale: Binds three specializations of absl::InlinedVector (a small-buffer-optimized vector) DIRECTLY (no wrappers), minted by ONE instantiate_ rule with explicit with_ tuples -- the corpus's with_ exercise (mixed type+NTTP tuples, allocator filled by default-argument substitution; a failing tuple hard-errors, the loud half of the with_/product_ contract): <int,4> and <double,2> (the prior listings -- identical reflections, the unchanged legacy suite proving with_ == explicit) plus the new <std::string,4> -> distinct Python types InlinedVectorInt4/InlinedVectorDouble2/InlinedVectorString4, with the full push_back/pop_back/at/operator[]/front/back/size/capacity/clear/empty/reserve/resize/erase/insert surface; differentially checked vs native Abseil incl. the small-buffer spill -> heap capacity growth (now also with a non-trivially-copyable element type). Links the prebuilt absl static lib (InlinedVector::at() -> ThrowStdOutOfRange). The hash/btree containers (flat_hash_map/set, btree_*) and FixedArray are DEFERRED to BINDER-0008: their public query/insert APIs are member templates (heterogeneous lookup) the binder skips, they transitively expose ~35 container_internal types under mangled names, and FixedArray hits an Abseil-internal AsValueType instantiation; a clean binding needs internal-namespace skipping + member-template handling.
skipped_features: flat_hash_map/flat_hash_set/btree_map/btree_set: bind+link OK but explode into container_internal types and their query APIs are member-template-only (BINDER-0008)
absl::FixedArray: Abseil-internal AsValueType<int> instantiation is ill-formed under the toolchain even after the array-member skip (BINDER-0008)
